offer.mapper.ts: OfferMapper.mapToDomain and OfferMapper.mapToOrm are the only places that map fields, including curierid <-> curierId
offer.repository.ts: findOfferById, findOfferByOrderId and saveOffer all return OfferMapper.mapToDomain(...); saveOffer uses OfferMapper.mapToOrm(offer)
offer.repository.ts: OfferRepository implements FindOfferByIdOutPort, FindOfferByOrderIdOutPort, SaveOfferOutPort, so it matches the domain port abstraction

parsedVerdict.reasoning: The three files handle one concern: persisting Offer aggregates. offer.orm-entity.ts defines the table schema (OfferOrmEntity). offer.mapper.ts is the single place that translates between the domain and ORM shapes (OfferMapper.mapToDomain / mapToOrm). offer.repository.ts implements the domain out-ports (FindOfferByIdOutPort, FindOfferByOrderIdOutPort, SaveOfferOutPort). Every read and write in the repository goes through OfferMapper; none of its methods map fields by hand, so the field-mapping rule exists only once. The repository also writes outbox messages through OutboxMapper.mapToORM in the same transaction as the offer save. That is the standard transactional-outbox pattern, and the outbox mapping rule stays in the shared relay module instead of being copied here. The local variable 'reportOrm' in saveOffer looks like a leftover name from copied code. That is a naming issue only, not a split in concerns or a bypassed abstraction.
